biography.plain_text: Slim Bouricha is a French engineer and entrepreneur based in Switzerland who founded the Beender energy group and Dutch shipbuilder Lynx Yachts. His businesses have spanned oil-and-gas engineering, petroleum investment and specialist vessel construction. He studied mechanical engineering at George Washington University and gained practical experience working in merchant marine shipyards early in his career.

long_biography.plain_text:
At Lynx Yachts, Slim Bouricha challenged a building process that separated design decisions from the shipyard responsible for executing them. He argued that reusing familiar specifications without questioning them could raise costs and compromise how a vessel worked. His approach put the customer’s intended use at the centre of the project.

The yard’s support-vessel range offered a practical expression of that thinking, providing additional capacity for equipment and activities alongside a main vessel. Bouricha established the business in Nijkerk, drawing on the Netherlands’ shipbuilding skills. Lynx and Outer Reef merged in 2024; the Dutch yard became a construction base for Outer Reef’s cruising boats.

uncertainties.detail: Beender sold its 40% Sfax venture stake to Panoro in April 2023 for cash and shares; the 2024 report still lists Beender among shareholders. Do not repeat that old direct Tunisian interest as current. Founder-control evidence and continuing Beender directorship support continuity, but a full private-portfolio allocation is unavailable. Investor and diversified were considered; neither is proven principal enough to displace the disclosed energy fallback.

Companies House records a French national resident in Switzerland, born June 1966, matching this uncommon name and source-record geography. Tunisian background is reported elsewhere, but no second nationality is inferred from origin. Exact birth day, middle names and birthplace remain unverified.

Exact-name/context searches covered Forbes, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, TikTok, Vimeo, Flickr, Wikipedia, personal and company websites. The Geneva Industrial & Financial LinkedIn result is plausible, but direct pages failed to open and no official cross-link was located, so it is omitted. Other profiles are namesake candidates. Company sites Lynx and Beender opened and match founder evidence. No verified personal site, Wikipedia or Forbes profile; Trip Advisor and Zillow irrelevant.

No supported family-transfer mechanism or material starting advantage was found. Self-made rests on positive founder-control evidence; silence is not used to infer an independent background. The family marine-engineering paragraph elsewhere on the Lynx team page belongs to another person and was not transferred.

Oil and gas and superyacht construction are defining operating sectors. Other investments lack sufficient evidence of a defining specialist identity and receive no tags. Personal vessel details and allegations are excluded.
